sceneFacts.proactivePrompt: Discover the surprising story behind this opening song.
sceneFacts.factHeader: "Perfect Day" was an unexpected opening for Legally Blonde.

factBeats.text: The upbeat pop song "Perfect Day" by Hoku kicks off Legally Blonde's opening sequence.
The song was originally intended to be the lead single from Hoku's second album.
Her record company decided to put the song on the Legally Blonde soundtrack to bolster excitement for her next album.
Hoku's label heads reportedly believed the film "wasn't going to become anything."

sceneFacts.factHeader: Elle's Arleen C sandals are more than just shoes.

factBeats.text: Elle Woods' closet in Legally Blonde is a vibrant display of early-2000s fashion.
Among her standout pieces are hot-pink python wedge sandals by Arleen C, featuring chunky platforms and blonde wood heels.
These playful shoes visually hint at how Elle brings her West Coast confidence to Harvard Law's rigid environment.
Costume designer Sophie de Rakoff used luxury brands like Arleen C for storytelling, making shoes "evidence" in Elle's world.

sceneFacts.proactivePrompt: See how Southern California campuses became Harvard Law?

factBeats.text: Harvard University permitted its name to be used in the film, but did not allow commercial filming on its actual campus.
The filmmakers first approached Stanford Law School, but it declined permission to film, not wanting its image tarnished.
USC also rejected the offer to use its name, stating there was "too much stereotyping" in the script for their liking.
Ironically, despite refusing to lend their names, both USC and UCLA campuses were used to film many of the Harvard-based scenes.
For example, the scene where Elle picks up her class schedule was filmed on the patio of UCLA's Kerckhoff Hall.

sceneFacts.proactivePrompt: Elle's colorful laptop made a bold statement.
sceneFacts.factHeader: Elle Woods' vibrant Mac stood out

factBeats.text: Elle Woods' orange Mac laptop helped her stand out in her Harvard Law classes.
The vibrant computer was part of Apple's "sherbet line" of products.
These early Macs were designed to be fluorescent and "screamed out at the audience."
The colorful Apple laptop made the "black monolithic borg machines" of her peers look "dowdy by comparison."

sceneFacts.proactivePrompt: Where is Paulette's salon located in real life?
sceneFacts.factHeader: Paulette's salon is a real Monrovia storefront.

factBeats.text: The exterior of Paulette's salon, Neptune's Beauty Nook, was filmed at a real storefront in Monrovia, California.
Viewers can find the actual building at 625 South Myrtle Avenue, east of Pasadena.
They considered various "weird directions" for the storyline, including the salon getting robbed.

sceneFacts.proactivePrompt: The 'Bend and Snap' has a wild origin story.
sceneFacts.factHeader: The 'Bend and Snap' was a spontaneous bar invention.

factBeats.text: The "Bend and Snap" move was not originally part of the film's script.
Producer Marc Platt wanted a secondary storyline for Paulette.
Co-writers Karen McCullah and Kirsten Smith considered crime plots, but they felt "tonally weird."
The idea for the "Bend and Snap" came to the writers during a drunken night at a Los Angeles bar.
Karen McCullah suggested Elle teach Paulette a move, and Kirsten Smith then demonstrated a version of the "Bend and Snap."

sceneFacts.proactivePrompt: Discover the choreographer behind this iconic move.
sceneFacts.factHeader: Toni Basil choreographed the iconic "Bend and Snap"

factBeats.text: The "Bend and Snap" move was first conceived by the writing team at a hotel bar in Beverly Hills.
Writer Kirsten Smith demonstrated the move by jumping off her barstool, and the team named it on the spot.
The now-iconic "Bend and Snap" move was choreographed by 80s icon and singer Toni Basil.
Toni Basil noted that despite being a short "one-and-a-half-minute number," it became an integral part of the film.

sceneFacts.proactivePrompt: What's the story behind Elle's pink courtroom dress?
sceneFacts.factHeader: Elle's pink dress: a statement of power

factBeats.text: Elle's courtroom look is head-to-toe pink, featuring a dress with a satin sash, cuffs, and lapels, along with sparkly sandals, a pink bag, lips, and nails.
Costume designers included subtle callbacks to traditional male suiting in the dress's cuffs and lapels, even adding sparkly cufflinks.
This vibrant pink stood out dramatically against the dark, mostly black attire of everyone else in the courtroom.
Costume designer Sophie de Rakoff intended for Elle to be her "most true self at this moment" in the film.
The outfit was a statement of confidence and self-knowledge, rejecting what the establishment expected of her.

sceneFacts.factHeader: Bruiser was played by a rescue dog named Moonie.

factBeats.text: The chihuahua who played Elle's beloved Bruiser was named Moonie.
Moonie was a canine actor adopted by trainer Sue Chipperton of Studio Animal Services.
Before his appearance in Legally Blonde, Moonie had been a rescue dog.
Moonie retired from acting in 2014, deciding at 15 years old he was too old to continue.
He passed away in March 2016 at the age of 18, with co-star Reese Witherspoon sharing a tribute.
